title: Edit Notes Pass smoke eval
objective: Task-specific eval for the Edit Notes Pass craftbook: five indexed clips and a raw transcript with a draggy middle (an interview tangent and a repeated demo step) become timestamped edit notes and a machine-readable cutlist that references only real footage within real durations.
prompt: footage for the workshop video is indexed and the trancript is in — can you do an edit pass and give me a cutlist? somethings draggy in the middle

setup.about: Self-contained eval project for edit-notes. The clip index is media/index.json (five clips with durations in seconds), the raw transcript is transcripts/raw.txt (per-clip mm:ss timecodes), and the storyboard is storyboard.md. The edit notes go to notes/edit-notes.md and the cut list to cutlist.json.
setup.missionObjectives: Use the Edit Notes Pass craftbook/template, review the seeded transcript against the media index, and produce timestamped edit notes plus cutlist.json. Every cut decision carries a timecode and a reason; no invented footage. No live services or real media tools — this is the review-and-cutlist half.

files.content:
Workshop video - raw transcript (rough auto pass, per-clip timecodes)

[c01-intro]
0:00 Welcome back to the workshop. Today we are building the dovetail jig I promised.
0:19 Quick look at the finished jig so you know where we are headed.
0:41 (dead air while the camera gets adjusted)

[c02-interview]
0:00 So the first thing people get wrong with dovetails is the layout, every time.
0:35 The story of my first jig - it was awful, but it cut straight, and that is the point.
1:20 ...and that reminds me of the time at the timber yard, there was this dog that guarded the offcuts bin... (long tangent, drifts well away from the jig)
2:40 Anyway, back to the jig. The key measurement is the pin width at the baseline.
2:58 If your pins are proud by even a millimeter, the joint telegraphs it.

[c03-broll-shop]
(no speech - bench shots, clamps closing, shavings falling, glue-up)

[c04-demo]
0:00 Set the fence to twelve degrees and lock it before anything else.
0:48 Now we cut the tails first. Watch the offcut side, not the blade.
1:22 Let me do that cut again from the other angle... (repeats the same step, adds nothing new)
1:50 (silent repositioning)
2:21 And the fit test - listen for that squeak. That squeak is the whole video.

[c05-outro]
0:00 If you build one, send me a photo. I read everything.
0:24 Next week: the box joint jig, which is somehow more controversial.

# Workshop video - storyboard

Shape: cold open on the finished jig, intro, expert interview for the why,
shop b-roll to breathe, the demo as the spine, outro with the ask.
Target: a tight six minutes. The interview and demo are allowed to flex,
but nothing stays in that does not earn its seconds.

success.summary: cutlist.json is a machine-readable record of real edit decisions: every row names a clip from media/index.json with in/out points and an action, the notes carry mm:ss timecodes and address the draggy middle, and the b-roll picture is considered.

checks.label: every cutlist row references a clip that exists in the media index
the edit notes carry mm:ss timecodes
the interview tangent in the middle is called out
the repeated demo step is called out

checks.rubric: Every in/out point in the cutlist sits within the referenced clip's duration from media/index.json, and the rows that trim or cut the middle correspond to the transcript's tangent (c02-interview around 1:20-2:40) and repeated demo step (c04-demo around 1:22-1:50) rather than arbitrary stretches.
checks.label: timecode precision and grounded cuts

axes.name: editorial-judgment
axes.description: Cuts and keeps serve the piece; the draggy middle is actually fixed, not just observed.

axes.name: timecode-precision
axes.description: In/out points are concrete, inside clip durations, and consistent between notes and cutlist.

axes.name: pacing-analysis
axes.description: The notes explain where energy dips and why, clip by clip.

axes.name: actionability
axes.description: An assembly step could execute the cutlist top to bottom without asking questions.
